name: Idiopathic Bilateral Vestibulopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Barany Society Diagnostic Criteria for Bilateral Vestibulopathy

criteria.description: Bilateral reduced or absent vestibular function documented by caloric testing, video head impulse test (vHIT), or rotary chair testing
Chronic imbalance and unsteadiness worsened in darkness or on uneven ground
No identifiable cause such as ototoxicity, infection, or autoimmune disease (idiopathic)
No evidence of central nervous system pathology on imaging or clinical examination

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral vestibular hypofunction confirmed by vestibular testing plus chronic imbalance symptoms without identifiable cause
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other known causes of bilateral vestibulopathy

imaging: Normal brain MRI excluding central causes of vestibular dysfunction
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; idiopathic etiology
other: Abnormal vestibular function tests: caloric testing, video head impulse test (vHIT), rotary chair testing

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe vertigo with neurological deficits
Progressive hearing loss suggesting alternative diagnosis
Signs of central nervous system involvement on examination or imaging
references: Strupp M, et al. Bilateral vestibulopathy: Diagnostic criteria consensus document of the Classification Committee of the Bárány Society. J Vestib Res. 2017;27(4):177-189.
Ward BK, et al. Bilateral vestibular hypofunction: Insights and clinical management. J Neurol. 2013;260(4):1037-1046.
